target_customer: Women buying premium hosiery direct to consumer, then retailers and licensing partners
problem: Pantyhose snag and run after a few wears. Sheertex knits sheer hosiery from ultra high molecular weight polyethylene fibers so it resists tearing.
business_model: Direct to consumer plus wholesale hosiery manufacturing with proprietary knit technology and in-house factory

founders.name: Katherine Homuth
founders.background_notes: Retail Insider (Feb 6, 2019) describes her as a software entrepreneur whose first company was ShopLocket. The YC page calls her a serial entrepreneur. She stepped down as CEO in 2025 as a condition of a financing and later launched Oomira.

technical_complexity.rationale: Knitting sheer fabric from UHMWPE ballistic-grade fiber required developing new materials and knitting processes and later its own factory, beyond ordinary apparel work.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary knit process and trademarks help, but hosiery incumbents could source fibers; the company later struggled to keep a lead when capital dried up.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying it. Instead the company ran into tariffs and financing trouble in 2025.

market_need_then: Fragile pantyhose is a widely known complaint. The company raised over $200,000 on Kickstarter in February 2018 per press releases seen in search results, showing consumer demand.

branding.domain_note: The srtxlabs.com site fetched during research served unrelated online casino content, so the parent company domain appears to have lapsed or been hijacked; not worked around.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold durability claims such as unbreakable pantyhose

branding.brand_signature: Unbreakable sheers positioning, Time Best Inventions of 2018 per search results

rebrands.why: Not stated in opened sources; Retail Insider (Feb 2019) says it was formerly Sheerly Genius and trademark filings for both names are dated April 2018

branding.community_and_virality: Kickstarter campaign and Time recognition in 2018 per search summaries; later stocking at retailers per an EDC article snippet.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear product promise and notable press in 2018 and 2019, but no evidence of a lasting community and the company struggled financially in 2025.

pivots.to: Sheertex brand and parent SRTX materials company
pivots.why: SRTX describes itself as building new materials and software for textiles beyond hosiery; exact date not stated

outcome_analysis: SRTX grew from a 2018 Kickstarter into a company that raised about $270M including debt by 2025 with a US$101M Series C in 2022, then ran into US tariffs, temporary layoffs of 40 percent of staff in February 2025 and a founder exit tied to a US$40M financing. In October 2025 it launched a strategic review that could end in a sale, with a second CEO departing and about 100 more layoffs. The directory status is Active, so no final exit is recorded, and the cause is capital-intensive manufacturing meeting a financing and tariff squeeze.
notes: Status is Active in the directory and a strategic review was announced 2025-10-30 with no sale found. One aggregator claims a buyer is absorbing the brand under insolvency protection; that source is weak and unconfirmed, and BNN states no creditor protection filing. The 2018 seed of $4M from Founders Fund, Valar and Gibraltar comes from a Globe and Mail mention in a search summary and a Seedtable page, and its date and amount are unverified. A WWD 2020 quote of a Series D bringing total funding to $44M conflicts with other labels and is not recorded. Totals conflict ($41M to $83M in CB Insights versus about $270M reported by BetaKit via company). BetaKit says the 2022 Series C was US$101M; the investors for it were not stated in the opened article. BetaKit says SRTX graduated from YC winter 2018 under the name Sheerly Genius. Homuth's departure month is March or April 2025 depending on source. Competitors left empty: no source dated near 2018 names rivals. Education not found.
